rules.name: T0 Run titles before the custom lexicon
rules.where: Phonemizer.phonemize, plus a new TextNormalizer.titles(_:) that moves the existing titles rule into it. The St. rules can stay where they are.
rules.trigger: Every title and suffix rule below (T1–T14). Run them on the raw text, right after TextNormalizer.linkLabels and before custom.mark, and only when normalization is on.
rules.reads_as: No reading of its own. It fixes the order the rules run in.
rules.risks: There are two problems today. (1) normalize(_:skippingMarkedSpans:) normalizes each plain stretch between lexicon marks on its own, so a title's lookahead can't see a name the lexicon has already marked. That is why 'Sen. Niamh Smyth' stays 'sen'. (2) The tech lexicon's case-insensitive CPL, ENS, SNR and LTS entries mark 'Cpl', 'Ens', 'Snr' and 'Lts' as letters first. NEW HAZARD: lexicon marks also hide non-names from today's title rule, so some cases are right only by accident. The tech entries 'alpha', 'X' and 'Echo Dot' hide them in 'Gen. Alpha', 'Gen. X' and '3rd Gen. Echo Dot'. Once T0 lands, all three turn into 'General …' unless T3 ships in the same change. Lexicon keys that start with a title word are 'Gen Digital' and 'Hon Hai'. Both have no period, and T4d never expands a title without one, so they're safe.

rules.name: T1 Name lookahead, shared by every title (tightened)
rules.where: TextNormalizer (replaces the current `name` lookahead used for Sen, Gov, Prof, Gen, Rep and Rev)
rules.trigger: Before the title: (?<![\p{L}\d.\-/]) (hyphen and slash are added, so 'Semi-Det.' and '2-Br.' don't count), and not directly after a digit and a space (?<!\d\s). After the title, the next word must be one of these: (a) A capitalised name with a lowercase second letter or an apostrophe (Smith, O'Brien, McKay, Pepper's). It must not be a usual sentence starter, it must not be on that title's skip list (T2), and it must NOT end in '.' unless it is itself a title from the table (Col., Gen., Sgt., Maj., Cmdr., Insp., Supt., Sec., Gov., Prof., Rev., Hon., Dr., Mr., Mrs., Ms., or Ltd. after Pvt./Pte.). (b) One or more initials (\p{Lu}\.\s?)+ followed by a name that doesn't end in '.' (J. T. Kirk). (c) For Sgt. only, an ordinal and 'Class'.
rules.reads_as: Not a reading; it gates T2–T4.
rules.risks: This is stricter than today's rule. A single capital letter (Col. B, Rev. B, Gen. Z), a digit (Gen. 2) and an all-caps word (Gen. AI) no longer count as names. The rule about a word ending in '.' fixes today's 'Phys. Rev. Lett.', which reads 'Reverend Lett.'. It also stops 'Ofc. Mgr.', 'Amb. Temp.', 'Br. Med. J.' and 'Br. J. Surg.' (initials followed by an abbreviation). The cost: 'Prof. Emer. Smith' won't expand unless 'Emer.' is added to the list. The number guard stops '30 Sec. Timer', '10 Reps.' and '2 Br. Condo', but not '1st Lt.', which is correct.

rules.name: T2 Titles with a period, before a name
rules.trigger: Matched case-sensitively: ABBR\. followed by T1's lookahead, after T3, T5, T7, T8, T9 and T14 have run. ABBR is one of: Lt, Capt, Col, Maj, Brig, Adm, Cmdr, Cdr, Ens, Sgt, Cpl, Pvt, Pte, Pfc, Spc, Det, Insp, Supt, Ofc, Fr, Msgr, Br, Hon, Pres, Amb, Atty, Sec, Mx, Mme, Mlle, plus the existing Sen, Gov, Prof, Gen, Rep and Rev. Plurals: Sens, Reps, Govs, Gens, Sgts, Lts, Capts, Cols, Pvts, Cpls, Dets, Profs, Revs, Drs. Skip lists (the next word stops the expansion): Lt before a body part (Arm, Leg, Knee, Hip, Hand, Foot, Eye, Ear, Shoulder, Ankle, Wrist, Elbow, Side, Lung, Kidney, Breast). Col before Total, Totals, Width, Header, Name or Springs. Brig directly after an ordinal ('2nd Brig.' is a brigade), or before Combat, Team or HQ. Adm before Fee, Fees, Free, Charge, Price, Ticket, Tickets, Assistant, Office, Staff, Building, Law, Code or Date. Amb before Temp, Temperature, Air, Noise, Light, Glass, Bottle, Jar, Service, Crew, Bay, Surgery or Care. Insp before Date, Due, Report, Cert, Certificate, Sticker, Fee, Type, Result, Results, Record, Form or Status. Det before Limit, Limits, House, Garage or Bungalow. Ofc before Hours, Supplies, Space, Phone, Use, Closed, Open, Manager, Address, Building, Number, Furniture, Equipment, Depot, Staff or Assistant. Fr before Fries, Toast, Onion, Bread, Dip, Vanilla, Roast, Press, Door, Doors, Polynesia, Guiana, Riviera, Quarter, Horn, Open, Revolution or Canadian. Br before Columbia, Honduras, Virgin, Manager, Office or Library. Pres before Church, Day, Sensor, Gauge, Switch, Valve, Deck, Slides or Notes. Sec before Deposit, Guard, Code or Level. Rev before Share, Growth, Limiter, Counter or Up. Rep directly after Czech, Dominican, Slovak or Dem. (Republic). Prof before Development, Services or Liability. Gov and Hon nouns go to T14 first.
rules.reads_as: Lieutenant, Captain, Colonel, Major, Brigadier, Admiral, Commander, Ensign, Sergeant, Corporal, Private (Pvt and Pte), Private First Class, Specialist, Detective, Inspector, Superintendent, Officer, Father, Monsignor, Brother, Honorable, President, Ambassador, Attorney, Secretary, Mix, Madame, Mademoiselle. Plurals: Senators, Representatives, Governors, Generals, Sergeants, Lieutenants, Captains, Colonels, Privates, Corporals, Detectives, Professors, Reverends, Doctors. Chains work without extra rules: Lt. Col., Brig. Gen., Lt. Cmdr., Det. Chief Insp., Rev. Dr., 1st Lt.
rules.risks: On skipped words the abbreviation is left exactly as today (a skip never invents another reading; T14 holds the few that do). Remaining false positives come from capitalised non-names that aren't on a skip list. They are most likely for Ofc. (office), Amb. (amber, ambulance), Pres. (pressure) and Sec. (security). Skip lists can't be complete, which is why the frozen cases test one word from each. Do not include 'Off.' ('Lights Off. Kids Asleep.') or 'M.' (an initial far more often than Monsieur). 'Cpl.', 'Ens.' and 'Lts.' need T0 or T13 to escape the tech lexicon.

rules.name: T3 Gen as a generation
rules.where: TextNormalizer.titles, before T2. Must ship together with T0.
rules.trigger: (a) (?<![\p{L}.])Gen\.(?=\s+(?:[XYZ]|Alpha|Beta)(?![\p{L}\d])). (b) Gen\. directly after an ordinal (\d+(st|nd|rd|th), First, Second, Third, Fourth, Fifth) or after Next, New, Last, Latest, Current, Previous, Prior, Older or Newer, with a space between.
rules.reads_as: 'Gen', without the period (unless it ends the sentence), so it reads 'jen'. 'Gen Z' without a period already reads 'jen zee'.
rules.risks: Fixes today's 'Our Next Gen. Platform' → 'Next General Platform'. Without (b), T0 would expose 'a 3rd Gen. Echo Dot' and 'Apple Pencil (2nd Gen.)' to the General reading. 'Gen. Admission' still reads General through T2, which is correct by coincidence.

rules.name: T4 UK titles without a period
rules.trigger: Case-sensitive whole words (?<![\p{L}\d.'’-])X(?=\s), followed by T1's lookahead and the same skip lists as T2. (a) Expand before a name: Lt, Capt, Cpl, Pte, Sgt, Cdr, Cmdr, Insp, Supt, Pfc, Revd, Cllr, Cllrs, Mx, Mme, Mlle, Prof, Fr. Extra skips: Fr is never expanded before Sa, Sat, Su or Sun, or after Th or Thu (calendar headers). Mx is never expanded before Plan (clinical management). (b) Expand only as a pair: Lt Col, Lt Gen, Lt Cdr, Lt Gov, Maj Gen, Brig Gen, Flt Lt, Sqn Ldr, Wg Cdr, Gp Capt, Ch Supt, Ch Insp, Det Insp, Det Sgt, Det Supt, Det Ch Supt, Rt Hon, Rt Revd, Rt Rev, Pvt Ltd, Pte Ltd. Also 'the Rev' before a name, unless the next word is 'Up'. (c) Col and Maj only before two capitalised name words (\s+\p{Lu}\p{Ll}+\s+\p{Lu}\p{Ll}). (d) Never expand Gen, Brig, Hon, Sec, Pres, Det (alone), Br, Off, Sen, Gov, Rep, Amb or Adm without a period.
rules.reads_as: Same words as T2, plus Flight Lieutenant, Squadron Leader, Wing Commander, Group Captain, Chief Superintendent, Chief Inspector, Detective Inspector, Detective Sergeant, Right Honourable, Right Reverend, Reverend (Revd), Councillor or Councillors (Cllr), Professor (Prof), Private Limited (Pvt Ltd, Pte Ltd).
rules.risks: 'Maj' moved from (a) to (c), because 'Maj Sjöwall' (a Swedish first name) read 'Major Sjöwall'. 'Maj Tim Peake' still expands. The calendar header 'Mo Tu We Th Fr Sa Su' read 'Father Sa Su' before the weekday skip. 'Brig Niagara' (a ship), 'Hon Hai' (a company), 'Gen Alpha', 'Gen Digital' and 'Col du Galibier' are protected by (c) and (d).

rules.name: T5 Sr, Jr, Snr, Jnr (rewritten)
rules.trigger: Jr., Jr and Jnr (case-sensitive, so not 'JR') read Junior wherever they stand as a whole word, because they have one meaning. For Sr., Sr and Snr: (a) After a name → Senior. The word before is capitalised and is not the sentence's first word or a usual sentence starter. 'Sr.' and 'Snr' may follow a comma ('Smith, Sr.'). Bare 'Sr' must follow the name after a single space, with no comma, and the word before must have at least 3 letters. That keeps element-symbol lists ('Ca, Sr, Ba', 'Rb Sr') out. (b) Before a job word or 'senior' noun anywhere in the next three capitalised words → Senior. The list: Engineer(s), Software, Product, Program, Project, Manager, Director, Vice, VP, Analyst, Developer, Designer, Consultant, Associate, Accountant, Architect, Scientist, Researcher, Editor, Writer, Counsel, Partner, Lecturer, Fellow, Specialist, Officer, Advisor, Adviser, Executive, Producer, Staff, Principal, Pastor, Minister, Chaplain, Nurse, Technician, Administrator, Coordinator, Recruiter, Attorney, Buyer, Planner, Strategist, Lead, Living, Center, Centre, Citizen(s), Discount, Housing, Care, High, Year, Class, Varsity, Team, Management. Lowercase 'sr.' before a lowercase word is also Senior. (c) 'Sr.' or 'Sr' (never 'Snr') before a female given name → Sister. Use a curated list that includes Mary, Marie, Maria, the initial 'M.', common English names (Helen, Anne, Catherine, Margaret, Teresa, Joan, Rose, Agnes, Bernadette, Clare, Frances, Elizabeth, Patricia, Kathleen, Dorothy, Monica, Cecilia, Josephine) and Irish names (Siobhán, Niamh, Bríd, Máire, Aoife). (b) wins if a job word follows. (d) Anything else: leave it alone ('Sr. No.' serial number, Spanish 'Sr. García').
rules.reads_as: (a) and (b): Senior. Jr forms: Junior. Keep a trailing period as the full stop when the abbreviation ends the sentence (the end of the text, or a usual sentence starter next), the same test the 'Street.' rule uses. A comma stays. (c): Sister.
rules.risks: As first written, (c) accepted any two capitalised words, so 'Sr. Business Analyst' (any job title with an unlisted first word) read 'Sister'. The given-name list fixes that and also keeps Spanish 'Sr. Juan Pérez' out. The cost: a nun with an unlisted name is left as 'S R'. Jr. reads 'junior' today only through the US fallback; the British voice gives ʤˈuːnjə, not the dictionary's ʤˈuːnɪə, so make it explicit. Bare 'Sr' already reads 'senior' everywhere from the dictionary (including 'Sr isotopes'); that is a science-pack issue, and T5 doesn't make it worse.

rules.name: T6 Esq
rules.reads_as: Esquire. Keep the period when it ends the sentence. A comma after it stays.
rules.risks: None found. 'Esq' has no other common meaning, and 'ESQ' in capitals isn't matched.

rules.name: T7 Assoc and Asst before a job
rules.trigger: (?<![\p{L}.])(Assoc|Asst)\.? before Prof., Prof, Professor, Dean, Director, Dir., Editor, Coach, Manager, Principal, Chief, Secretary, Sec. or Attorney. Don't fire when the word before is capitalised and isn't the sentence's first word.
rules.reads_as: Associate or Assistant. The 'Prof.' after it then expands under T2.
rules.risks: 'Dental Assoc. Director Kim' (Association) is protected by the rule about the word before (frozen case). 'Asst. Colors' (assorted) and 'Assoc. Press' are never followed by a job word, so they stay.

rules.name: T8 Pairs that don't need a name
rules.trigger: 'Treas. Sec.' or 'Treas Sec'. 'Hon. Sec.', 'Hon Sec', 'Hon. Treas.'. 'Maj.' before Leader or Whip. 'Sgt. Maj.' always ('Sgt. Maj. of the Army'). 'Sgt. at Arms' or 'Sgt.-at-Arms'. Rank pairs expand even with no name after them: Lt. Gov., Lt. Col., Lt. Gen., Maj. Gen., Brig. Gen., Atty. Gen., Sec. Gen. or Sec.-Gen. 'Rt. Rev.' and 'Rt. Hon.' with periods. 'Lt. j.g.' or 'Lt. (j.g.)'. 'Sr. Sec.' or 'Sr Sec' before School, Schools or Education. A title joined to '-elect' before a name: Gov.-elect, Pres.-elect, Sen.-elect, Rep.-elect.
rules.reads_as: Treasury Secretary. Honorary Secretary. Honorary Treasurer. Majority. Sergeant Major. Sergeant at Arms. Lieutenant Governor, Lieutenant Colonel, Lieutenant General, Major General, Brigadier General, Attorney General, Secretary General. Right Reverend, Right Honourable. Lieutenant junior grade. Senior Secondary. Governor-elect, President-elect, Senator-elect, Representative-elect.
rules.risks: 'Hon. Member' (Parliament) stays Honourable under T2, which is correct. 'Treas.' alone before a name isn't expanded; it's rare and ambiguous between Treasurer and Treasury. 'Sr. Sec.' needs this pair because T2 alone read 'Sec. School' as 'Secretary School'.

rules.name: T9 Lt meaning light
rules.trigger: (?<![\p{L}.])[Ll]t\.?(?=\s+(?i:blue|pink|purple|yellow|teal|aqua|beige|khaki|lavender|turquoise|peach|orange|lilac|mint|cream|taupe|duty|wash|roast)\b). Also before olive, coral, rose, amber, ruby, jade, hazel or violet, but only when no capitalised word follows the colour ('Color: Lt. Olive' is light; 'Lt. Olive Harper' is Lieutenant).
rules.reads_as: light (so 'Lt. Blue' reads 'light Blue' and 'Lt. Duty Casters' reads 'light Duty Casters')
rules.risks: As first written, the list included 'olive' and 'coral' unconditionally, so 'Lt. Olive Harper' read 'light Olive Harper'. Colours that are also common surnames (Brown, Gray, Grey, Green, White, Black) are still left out, so 'Lt. Gray' stays Lieutenant. That reading is wrong on product pages ('Lt Grey Marl') but right in news. A later option is to read them 'light' after 'Color:' or 'Colour:'. Optional rule; see the open question.

rules.name: T10 Ret after a name
rules.trigger: \((?:Ret|ret)\.?\) anywhere, or ', Ret.' or ', ret.' after a capitalised word and before a comma, a closing bracket or the end of the clause.
rules.risks: Very low. In brackets, 'Ret.' has no other common meaning. 'Ret. Policy' isn't in brackets and doesn't follow a comma, so it stays.

rules.name: T11 A rank with no name after it (optional, narrowed)
rules.trigger: One of Sgt., Capt., Cpl., Pvt., Pfc., Spc., Cmdr. or Supt., directly after (?i:the|a|to|as|our|his|her|their|my|your|new|former|then) and a space, where T1 doesn't match. Lt. only after 'to' or 'as' ('promoted to Lt.', 'served as Lt.').
rules.reads_as: The rank word ('promoted to Sergeant', 'ask the Captain'). Keep the period when it ends the sentence.
rules.risks: As first written, Insp. and Lt. after 'the' were on the list. That gave 'the Inspector results' (inspection) and 'the Lieutenant version' (light version); both are now frozen cases. Col. (column), Maj. (majority), Gen., Det., Sec., Insp. and Pres. stay off the list. Depends on the open question about ranks with no name.

rules.name: T12 Keep a title and its name in one sentence (app chunking)
rules.where: Tokenizer.titles, which also feeds runOnTitles and Tokenizer.split; TextPrep.chunks
rules.trigger: Add every T2 title with its period, the plurals (Lts., Sgts., Sens., Drs. …), Sr., Jr., Rt. and Msgr., and the T4 no-period titles that end a word ('Revd', 'Cllr') where splitting matters. I re-ran NLTokenizer myself: it splits after Det., Fr., Sr., Mx., Hon., Brig., Gen. (after Brig.), Msgr., Rt., Lts., Sgts. and Drs., even before a name. It doesn't split after Lt., Sgt., Capt., Jr., 'Pvt. Ltd.', Cllr or 'Gov.-elect'.
rules.reads_as: Not a reading. TextPrep joins the halves again through titleContinues, so the title reaches the phonemizer with its name and expands.
rules.risks: The --speech-test harness phonemizes whole lines, so it can't see this bug. Add TextPrep.chunks tests such as 'Det. Benson called.' and 'Rt. Rev. Hollis preached.', each giving one chunk. Suffixes are safe to add too: 'Sr.' before 'He' still ends the sentence, because 'He' is a usual sentence starter. Note that 'Drs.' isn't in runOnTitles today.

rules.name: T13 Tech lexicon case clashes
rules.trigger: The entries CPL, ENS, SNR and LTS are case-insensitive today.
rules.reads_as: Make them match exactly (all capitals only). Clashes: Cpl. is corporal, Ens. is ensign, Snr is senior (UK), Lts. is lieutenants. 'Our CPL fell', 'ENS names' and 'The SNR was poor' keep their letters (frozen cases).
rules.risks: Lowercase 'snr' in code or maths would no longer get the letters; it's usually inside an identifier anyway. Separately, the tech lexicon reads 'Ltd' as lˈɪmɪtɪd in the US voice, while the dictionary reads 'limited' as lˈɪməTᵻd. That's harmless, but it's why the 'Pvt. Ltd.' case is British-voice only.

rules.name: T14 Readings that don't need a name (new)
rules.trigger: (a) Atty./Atty in any case, as a whole word. (b) Pvt./Pvt in any case, as a whole word ('Pvt. Parking', 'pvt. room'). (c) Hon. before Mention or Mentions. (d) Hon. before Doctorate, Degree, Fellow, Fellowship, Lecturer, Consul, Life, Citizen, Chair, Chairman, President, Director, Advisor, Secretary or Treasurer (the last two are covered by T8). (e) Gov. before Shutdown, Website, Site, Agency, Agencies, Contract, Contracts, Contractor, Contractors, Funding, Grant, Grants, Job, Jobs, Official, Officials, Employee, Employees, Worker, Workers, Data, Bond, Bonds, Debt, Spending, Program, Programs, Programme, Policy or ID.
rules.reads_as: (a) attorney, with the capital kept when written with one. (b) private. (c) Honorable. (d) Honorary. (e) Government.
rules.risks: Each word has only one meaning in these positions, so this isn't guessing. (e) fixes today's 'The Gov. Shutdown' → 'Governor Shutdown'. 'Gov. Office' and 'Gov. Building' are left out on purpose ('the Governor's office' is just as likely). 'Hon. Professor' is left out ('The Hon. Professor Smith' exists). Not adopted: Rev. as revenue ('Rev. Share' reads 'rev' after the skip), Rep. as Republic, Prof. as professional, Fr. as French, Sec. as security, Insp. as inspection and Det. as detached. Those are skipped only (T2); see the open question.

rules.name: T15 All-caps military ranks stay letters (no rule)
rules.where: None (a decision, recorded so nobody adds the rule)
rules.trigger: US Army, Navy and Marines official forms: SGT, SSG, CPT, LTC, COL, MAJ, PFC, SPC, 1LT, CAPT, CDR, ADM, GEN.
rules.risks: They collide with common acronyms: CPT (billing codes), LTC (long-term care), COL (cost of living), SPC (process control) and PFC (perfluorocarbons). A military field pack can read them before a name. Frozen cases 'CPT codes', 'LTC insurance' and 'DCI Barnaby' guard it.

open_questions: 'Sr.' before a name: should it read 'Sister'? I recommend 'Sister' only before a female given name from a curated list (Mary, Helen, Siobhán … or 'M.'), and never when a job word follows within three words. Otherwise leave it as letters. 'Senior' always applies after a name or before a job word. The original 'any two capitalised words' test made 'Sr. Business Analyst' read 'Sister'.

A rank with no name after it ('She was promoted to Sgt.', 'Ask the Capt. about it'): expand it, or leave it? Today these read 'S G T' and 'capt'. I recommend expanding only Sgt., Capt., Cpl., Pvt., Pfc., Spc., Cmdr. and Supt. after 'the', 'a', 'to', 'as' or a possessive, and Lt. only after 'to' or 'as'. Insp. after 'the' is usually inspection, and Lt. after 'the' is often 'light'.

A bare 'Lt.' that is neither before a name nor a colour ('the Lt. version', 'Lt. Knee') reads 'limit' today, which is wrong in every sense. Should Core spell it 'L T' instead (soldiers also say 'the L T')? I recommend yes. Two frozen cases would then be re-frozen.

'Lt.' before a colour on product pages ('Color: Lt. Blue', 'Lt. Duty Casters'): read it 'light'? I recommend yes, for colours that aren't common surnames and for Duty, Wash and Roast. Leave 'Lt. Gray', 'Lt. Brown' and 'Lt. Green' as Lieutenant, unless they come right after 'Color:' or 'Colour:'.

Title abbreviations with a plain non-title meaning that the next word settles: 'Fr. Fries' (French), 'Sec. Deposit' (security), 'Insp. Date' (inspection), 'Semi-Det. House' (detached), 'Rev. Share' (revenue or 'rev'), 'Czech Rep.' (Republic), 'Prof. Development' (professional). Should Core read them, or only stop the wrong title (as specified now, frozen)? I recommend reading 'French', 'security' and 'inspection' in their pairs. Leave 'Rev. Share' as 'rev', since 'rev share' is common speech, and leave 'Lt. Knee' (left) to the medical pack. Only 'Gov. Shutdown' (Government) and 'Hon. Doctorate' (Honorary) are in the speech cases now.

British voice, 'Gen Z': 'Gen Zed' or 'Gen Zee'? Usage is split. The letter is 'zed' in the UK, but 'Gen Zee' is spreading among young British speakers, and the British dictionary reads Z as 'zee' today. I made the 'Gen. Z' case US-only. If the letters area settles on 'zed', add says_gb 'Jen Zed'.
'Mx': 'mix' or 'mux'? I recommend 'mix'. Merriam-Webster lists it first, and surveys of people who use the title put it first.
'Pfc.': 'Private First Class' or the letters 'P F C', as soldiers often say it? I recommend 'Private First Class', the way a newsreader reads AP copy.

'Col. A' or 'Col. B' in spreadsheets and tables: read 'column A'? I recommend leaving it as it is ('coll B') in Core, because a single letter isn't enough to be sure. A data or spreadsheet pack could read it 'column'.

Party and state after a lawmaker ('Sen. Elizabeth Warren (D-Mass.)'): today read 'D Mass'. This is outside my area. I recommend a follow-up rule that reads it 'Democrat of Massachusetts', using the state abbreviations the addresses area already has.
review_notes: How it was checked: every speech case and all 60 frozen cases ran through --speech-test and --phonemize in both voices, using a scratch copy outside the repo (no repo file was edited). Today 13 of 188 speech checks pass. They pass in both voices for Msgr., Rev. Jesse Jackson, Ms. Patel, Gen. Alpha and 3rd Gen. Echo Dot, and in the US voice only for Rev. Dr. … King Jr., Sammy Davis Jr and Tom Hale Jnr. All 120 frozen readings stayed identical across a freeze and a second run.

I checked every new 'says' sentence with --phonemize. Three real names the stack misreads were swapped, because the instructions say to pick other wording: 'Vindman' (read like 'vined'; the case became the email greeting 'Dear Lt. Col. Ramirez,'), 'Mei' (read 'my'; now 'Laura Chen') and 'Budde' (read 'bud'; now an invented bishop, 'Anne Hollis'). Governor-elect, Honorary, Monsignor, Secondary, Mademoiselle, Lieutenants, Weimer, Thune, Spanberger and Barnaby all read correctly. The British voice gives 'Lieutenant' as lɛftˈɛnənt and reads 'Honorable' and 'Honourable' the same way.

Hard rules: no digits, symbols, Roman numerals or written abbreviations in any 'says'. 'Jen' and lowercase 'rev' stand for the clipped words people actually say ('Gen', 'rev'). They carry no period or capital, so no title rule can touch them.

Expectations changed: 'Gen. Z' is now US-only. British usage is split between 'Gen Zed' and 'Gen Zee', and the expected British reading depended on another area's open decision. 'Senate Maj. Leader' now names John Thune, the current majority leader, not Schumer. 'Hon. mention' moved from frozen to speech ('Honorable mention'), because every reader expands it and freezing would have locked in 'hun mention'. 'Color: Lt. Blue' now says 'light Blue' so that the rest of the line matches the text exactly.

Removed as redundant: Staff Sgt., Sgt. Maj. Tom Hale, Col. Mustard, Det. Sgt., Sqn Ldr, Sr. Engineer, Jr. Developer, and 'Martin Luther King Jr. spoke first.'. Each tests the same path as a case kept. 'Rev. Share' was drafted and dropped as ambiguous ('rev share' or 'revenue share'). Frozen cases dropped as weaker duplicates: Mr. Smith, PhD without periods, CPA, the brig, 'The major said no', Junior year, Chief Joseph, Field Marshal, Col. A, Adm. Free and Amb. Temp.

Rule attacks: 26 new frozen near misses. Each one would have been rewritten wrongly by a rule as first written: Semi-Det. (T2 hyphen), Main Ofc. Closed, Ofc. Mgr., Lt. Knee, Br. Manager, Amb. Glass, Oil Pres. Sensor, Pres. Deck, Sec. Deposit, Adm. Assistant, 2nd Brig. Combat Team (T2), the calendar 'Fr Sa Su', Mx Plan, Maj Sjöwall, the Rev Up Tour (T4), Insp. results and Lt. version (T11), and Sr. No. (T5). There are also case and caps guards (JR Pass, CPT, LTC, DCI), the T7 'Dental Assoc.' guard, 'Gen. AI' and 'Gen AI', and '2 Br. Condo'. Speech cases that the first-draft rules would have got wrong: 'Sr. Business Analyst' (Sister), 'Sr. Sec. School' (Secretary), 'Hon. Doctorate' (Honorable), 'Lt. Olive Harper' (light) and 'Lt. Duty' (Lieutenant). All the rules were tightened to match.

Existing false positives found beyond 'Gen. Z' and 'Rev. B': 'Next Gen. Platform' → General, 'Gov. Shutdown' → Governor, 'Phys. Rev. Lett.' → Reverend Lett., 'Rev. Share' → Reverend, 'Prof. Development Day' → Professor, and 'Dem. Rep. Congo' and 'Czech Rep. Team' → Representative. The first two are speech cases. The rest are covered by T1 (a word ending in '.' must be a title) and the T2 skip lists. They aren't speech cases because the right reading is ambiguous, or because it needs another area ('Phys.' itself is misread as 'fize').

T0 hazard: lexicon marks hide words from today's title rule. 'Gen. Alpha', 'Gen. X' and '3rd Gen. Echo Dot' are right today only because the tech entries 'alpha', 'X' and 'Echo Dot' mask them. Running titles first exposes them, so T3 (generation, now with the ordinal and 'Next' guard) has to land in the same change. The tech LTS entry also clashes with 'Lts.' (added to T13).

Positives added for real-world text: an email greeting (Dear Lt. Col. Ramirez), a letter to a nun (Dear Sr. Helen), a job ad (Sr. Business Analyst), a church bulletin (Sr. Pastor), an Indian school (Sr. Sec. School), a sign (Pvt. Parking Only), a legal brief (atty. fees), award results (Hon. mention, Hon. Doctorate), news (Gov.-elect, the Lt. Gov., Sgt. Maj. of the Army, Rt. Rev., Det. Chief Insp., Lts.), a product listing (3rd Gen. Echo Dot, Lt. Duty Casters) and a UK academic (Snr Lecturer). Regression guards kept or added: Rev. Jesse Jackson, Ms. Patel, Msgr. (passes only through the fallback model) and the Gen generation cases.

T12 re-measured with my own NLTokenizer run. It confirms splits after Det., Fr., Sr., Mx., Hon., Brig. and then Gen., Msgr., Rt., Lts., Sgts. and Drs., and no split after Lt., Sgt., Capt., Jr., Cllr or Gov.-elect.

Frozen cases that lock in a poor reading today ('Br.' read 'br' or a bare 'b', 'Fr.' read 'fr', 'Det.' read 'dit', 'Insp.' read 'insp', 'Lt.' read 'limit', 'Mx' read 'mex') are there to stop a wrong title expansion. If a later letters or field rule improves them on purpose, re-freeze them; their notes say so.

Bare 'Sr' (strontium) already reads 'senior' everywhere from the dictionary ('We measured Sr isotopes'). That's not a title issue, so no case was added. T5's stricter rule for bare 'Sr' (no comma, a word of 3+ letters before it) makes sure element lists don't get worse.
